title: The Voynich Manuscript
hook: This 240-page book is written in a mysterious language nobody has ever understood.

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: This handwritten manuscript is filled with strange plants, symbols, and diagrams.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: Radiocarbon dating places the vellum's creation between 1404 and 1438.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: Its pages show unfamiliar plants that don't match any known species on Earth.

beats.label: CLUE 3
beats.line: One section shows zodiac signs ringed by tiny figures, but their meaning is unknown.

beats.label: THEORY
beats.line: Many experts think it may be an elaborate hoax, or a constructed invented language.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: Despite decades of effort by codebreakers, not one page has ever been translated.

end.line: Will the Voynich manuscript ever be decoded?

description: The Voynich manuscript is a 15th-century book written in an unknown script, filled with strange plants and diagrams nobody has ever explained. Despite a century of attempts, not one page has been reliably translated.

facts.claim: The Voynich manuscript is an illustrated codex of about 240 vellum pages written in an unknown script that has never been deciphered.
Radiocarbon dating in 2009 placed the vellum's creation between 1404 and 1438.
facts.source: Wikipedia: Voynich manuscript; Yale University 2009 dating

facts.claim: Its illustrations include unidentified plants, astronomical diagrams, and images of bathing women, in sections often called herbal, astronomical, and biological.
The manuscript was purchased by antique book dealer Wilfrid Voynich in 1912, after whom it is named.
Numerous linguists, cryptographers, and computer scientists have attempted to decode it; no proposed solution is widely accepted.
Some researchers argue it may be an elaborate hoax or a constructed language rather than a genuine coded text.
It has been held at Yale University's Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library since 1969.
